transcript: Great question. I think you have to look even beyond the House. One of the battles I expect will be as we talk about the corporate rate. Eight years ago when the corporate rate was at 35%, I think there was uniform. belief, not just consensus, but we all felt that the rate had to come down for the United States to be competitive, United States companies to be competitive. We have to make sure that whatever we do keeps American companies competitive. There is, since the passage of the last bill, there has been an international effort through the OECD to stop the race to the bottom, where so many countries were trying to entice especially American companies with low or even zero tax rates. Secretary Yellen negotiated, and we have this goal of getting a minimum 15 percent international tax rate. So we end that race to the bottom. Republicans don't want to engage in that. They're saying the United States can go it alone. And what we're seeing is around the world countries are already moving forward. If anyone would have predicted that South Korea would be one of the first or the first to move, I don't think anyone had that on their bingo card, but yet that's what happened and we're seeing it in Europe and in Japan. And the United States is competing in a global economy. So I think one of the fights will be how do we make sure that U.S. companies are competitive on a global stage, but that the United States is engaging with our allies and countries around the world so that other countries aren't in a position to tax U.S. companies and tax dollars that should be in the U.S. are actually being paid outside. What we've seen certainly with the Trump administration and the potential of a new Trump administration, tax cuts that help only the people who are the most successful have accumulated the most wealth. Part of what the American dream is is for every American to have the chance to pursue whatever career they want to do to create some financial security in their life and have retirement security at the end of their career. And that's where I think you'll see the Democrats really focusing.
